comments.body:
## RCA — confirmed root cause (Phase 1 complete)

Reproduced live (unauthenticated, no credential sent), 2026-08-27:

    $ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp/
    HTTP/2 307
    location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp

    $ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -X POST -d '{}' https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp
    HTTP/2 401   (www-authenticate: Bearer ...)

Neither response carried `strict-transport-security`. Symptoms confirmed as reported.

### Two mechanisms, both proven at runtime

**A — why a redirect exists at all.** `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:127` is a PREFIX
`location /mcp` with a URI-preserving `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;` (no path). The external
`/mcp/` therefore reaches the app verbatim as `/mcp/`, while the app mounts its
Streamable-HTTP endpoint at `http_path = "/mcp"` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:524`, handed to
`FastMCP(streamable_http_path=path)` at `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:618-627`). Starlette's router
default `redirect_slashes=True` (set nowhere in this repo) then emits the 307 `/mcp/` -> `/mcp`.

The redirect is emitted by the APP, not by nginx — nginx emits 301s for its own directory
redirects, never a 307, and it has no rewrite in that block.

`docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271` already prescribes the correct edge for exactly this asymmetry —
EXACT-MATCH `location = /mcp/` and `location = /mcp`, both `proxy_pass .../mcp` — and states
the reason: "The external edge is `/mcp/` but the app serves `http_path = \"/mcp\"`". The
committed template diverged from its own documented pattern.

**B — why the redirect target is plaintext.** nginx does send `proxy_set_header
X-Forwarded-Proto https;` (`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:132`), yet the production Location
is `http://`. That live response is direct proof that the forwarded proto is being IGNORED by
the app. Mechanism: uvicorn is constructed at `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:311-317` with no
`forwarded_allow_ips`; uvicorn then defaults it from the environment —
`uvicorn/config.py:356-357`, `os.environ.get("FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS", "127.0.0.1")` — and wraps
the app in `ProxyHeadersMiddleware(trusted_hosts=...)` at `uvicorn/config.py:527`. The MCP app
runs INSIDE a container (`docker-compose.yml:337` `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST: "0.0.0.0"`, published
`127.0.0.1:8091:8091`), so nginx's connection arrives from the docker bridge gateway, not
`127.0.0.1`; the peer is untrusted, `X-Forwarded-Proto` is dropped, `scope["scheme"]` stays
`http`, and every app-generated absolute URL is built as `http://`. No `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`
is set anywhere in `infra/`.

**C — no backstop.** A repo-wide grep for `strict-transport` over `infra/ docs/ src/ tests/`
returns ZERO hits. The 443 server block (`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:77-158`) has no
`add_header Strict-Transport-Security`.

### The discriminating experiment

In-process, over the real `streamable_http_app()`, POST `/mcp/` with `follow_redirects=False`:

    E1  bare app                       -> 307  Location: http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp
    E2  ProxyHeadersMiddleware(trusted_hosts="127.0.0.1"),
        peer 172.17.0.1, X-Forwarded-Proto: https
                                       -> 307  Location: http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp
    E3  ProxyHeadersMiddleware(trusted_hosts="*"),
        peer 172.17.0.1, X-Forwarded-Proto: https
                                       -> 307  Location: https://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp

E1 confirms mechanism A: the APP emits the 307 (kills "nginx generated it").
E2 reproduces the exact production symptom.
E2 vs E3 is the discriminator: the ONLY difference is the trusted-peer setting, and it flips
the scheme. That kills the alternatives "the app hardcodes http", "nginx rewrote the Location",
and "HTTP/2 stripped the scheme".

### Defect legitimacy: `defect`

Cited authority the behaviour violates:
- `docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271` — the documented exact-match edge pattern this template does not
  implement, written specifically to reconcile `/mcp/` with `http_path=/mcp`.
- `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_TLS_AT_EDGE=true` (`docker-compose.yml:340`; gate at
  `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:560-566`) is a design invariant that the deployment is https-only
  with TLS terminating at nginx. A 307 to `http://` on the documented client URL contradicts it.
- The `static` bearer-PAT auth design: a 307 preserves method and body, and clients differ on
  retaining `Authorization` across a same-host scheme change.

### Defect origin — `caused_by` fd4a-4e91-f179-4932 (cibophobic-holohedral-esok)

`git blame -w -C -M -L 118,140 -- infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` puts the `location /mcp` +
`proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;` lines on **8297083532a3** ("Add rebar-mcp HTTP service to the AWS
box"), trailer `rebar-ticket: fd4a-4e91-f179-4932`. That single change introduced BOTH halves:
the prefix location that diverges from the doc's exact-match pattern, and the containerised MCP
service that never set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`. Its own AC3 says "nginx `/mcp/` proxies to a named
`upstream rebar_mcp`" and its oracle was a structural parse — which asserted the upstream wiring
but nothing about scheme, trailing slash, or redirect behaviour, so the divergence escaped.

Divergence from a whole-file blame majority, recorded per protocol: `git blame` attributes
`proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;` (line 132) to **6cd6f4e1f7c0c** (Iso Tester,
2026-06-29, the original TLS terminator). That line is CORRECT and is not the defect — the
defect is that the containerised consumer added by fd4a never met the obligation to trust it.
Attributing to 6cd6f4e1 would be the unmet-obligation misattribution the protocol warns about.

The **HSTS omission (C) is older** than fd4a — it is scope-of-work of the original TLS
terminator `6cd6f4e1f7c0c` — but fd4a is what created the bearer-PAT-over-plaintext exposure
that makes it P1, so the bug attributes to fd4a and the HSTS gap is fixed here as part of the
same edge hardening.

Phase 2 (RED -> GREEN) follows. Ticket will NOT be closed in this session.

comments.body:
## Blast-radius check on root cause B — narrower than feared, stated explicitly

Root cause B is `forwarded_allow_ips` defaulting to `127.0.0.1` in a container, which makes
uvicorn distrust EVERY forwarded header from nginx, not just the proto. That is broader than a
redirect bug in principle, so I checked the two places it would plausibly hurt most rather than
assuming the redirect was the whole story. Both came back clean, and the honest answer is that
the reachable impact is bounded:

**1. RFC 9728 metadata and the `WWW-Authenticate` `resource_metadata` URL — NOT affected.**
These are built from the configured `auth_resource_server_url`
(`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:610`, fed by `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL` in
`docker-compose.yml:347`), not from the request scheme. Confirmed empirically against the live
box: the unauthenticated 401 returns
`resource_metadata="https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`
— `https`, despite `scope["scheme"]` being `http` at that moment. Config-derived absolute URLs
are structurally immune to this defect.

**2. Client-IP-keyed logic — none exists in rebar.** A search of `src/rebar/` for
`request.client`, `scope["client"]`, `remote_addr` and `X-Forwarded-For` consumers returns no
matches, so no rebar logging, rate limiting, or audit path keys on the peer address and none is
silently recording the docker bridge gateway. (uvicorn's own access log does show the gateway,
but that is uvicorn's log line, not rebar logic, and it is corrected by the same
`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` fix.)

**Conclusion.** The only reachable instance of the defect is a scheme-derived absolute URL, and
the slash-redirect `Location` was the one such URL the app actually emits today. So the reported
bug WAS the blast radius — this is not a redirect symptom of a larger live exposure.

**The residual risk is forward-looking, not current:** any future code that reads
`request.url`, `request.client`, or builds a URL from the request rather than from config would
silently inherit the plaintext scheme. Fixing B here (rather than only patching the edge) is what
removes that trap, which is the main reason it is in scope alongside the nginx change.

## Step 7 parity sweep

**Axis 1 (construct sweep): no siblings.** The construct is "external path with a trailing slash
proxied URI-preserving to an app mounted at the slash-less path". `/review/` uses a
prefix-stripping `proxy_pass .../;` and `/opcert/` preserves a prefix the app genuinely serves,
so neither has the asymmetry. No other instance in the tree.

**Axis 2 (parity census): three MISSING slots, dispositioned by ticket.** The rule this fix
enforces — an https request must never receive a Location that downgrades to `http` — now holds
for the MCP paths only. `/review/` (`:92`), `/opcert/` (`:107`) and Gerrit's `location /`
(`:152`) have no equivalent guarantee. I deliberately did NOT hoist `proxy_redirect` to the
server level to cover them: it defaults to `default`, derived from each location's own
`proxy_pass`, so a server-level rule would replace `/review/`'s prefix-stripping rewrite and
could break its relative redirects. Filed as
**a61d-adf9-3725-4847 (enchanting-phantastic-weevil)**, linked `discovered_from` this bug.

HSTS is NOT part of that gap — it is added at the 443 **server** level here, so all four
surfaces inherit it immediately.

## Phase 2 complete — fix committed locally (NOT pushed, ticket NOT closed)

Local commit **e9cec6bad8d1684150f4e8e2769e2d0fe1fa398f** on branch `79b2-mcp-https-redirect`,
authored `RebarBotNava <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>`, signed off, `rebar-ticket:` trailer
verified (`verify-commit-ticket: OK - resolved 79b2-6ebc-6c1d-4125`). 4 files, +280/-7.

### RED -> GREEN, held out

All 5 new tests were observed RED **before** any fix existed, each failing for its own specific
missing artifact (`exact-match location = /mcp/ block not found`, `no add_header
Strict-Transport-Security "..." always;`, `the mcp service must set FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS...`,
`KeyError: 'FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS'`) — not import or fixture errors. The tests were then removed
from the tree entirely (saved as a patch) before the fix subagent was launched, and the agent
was told the paths were off-limits. It never saw them. Re-applied afterwards: **60 passed**.
Broader sweep over the infra/mcp/deploy/opcert suites: **369 passed, 6 skipped**.

### Mutation check — 6 seeded defects, all killed, run under `sandbox-exec`

    RED   M1 drop the exact-match locations          (cause A)
    RED   M2 drop proxy_redirect                     (edge backstop)
    RED   M3 drop the HSTS header                    (cause C)
    RED   M4 drop FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS  [structural]  (cause B)
    RED   M4 drop FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS  [behavioural] (cause B)
    RED   M5 pin FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS to 172.17.0.1   (the plausible wrong value)

M5 matters most: it is the fix that *looks* right and silently re-opens the downgrade when the
bridge address drifts. The sandbox denied writes outside the worktree in a live probe before the
run (and twice refused my own backup paths, which is how I know it was actually enforcing).

### The fix

`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` — exact-match `location = /mcp/` and `= /mcp`, both
`proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp/mcp;`, each carrying the full SSE settings and forwarded headers (an
exact-match location inherits nothing from the prefix one); the prefix `location /mcp` retained
unchanged for `/mcp/...` sub-paths; `proxy_redirect http://$host/ https://$host/;` plus the
named-upstream form in all three MCP locations; `add_header Strict-Transport-Security
"max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;` at 443 server level.

`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: "*"` on the `mcp` service. No `src/`
change: uvicorn reads the variable natively.

### Verification output

    make lint      EXIT=0
    make typecheck EXIT=0   (mypy: Success: no issues found in 677 source files)

### Fix-safety audit

No `src/` change, no docs/examples change, no new dependency, no test weakened. One pre-existing
test — `test_nginx_mcp_location_proxies_to_the_named_upstream` — needed its **selector**
tightened: `location\s+/mcp\b[^{]*\{` matched the words `location /mcp` inside a COMMENT and then
ran forward to the next `{`, capturing an exact-match block. Now anchored to a line-leading
directive. All three assertions are byte-identical, and I proved it is a selector fix rather than
a weakening by reverting the config and confirming the tightened test **passes against the
pre-fix template too** — which it must, since the prefix location's behaviour is unchanged.

### EXPECTED_URL decision: unchanged, and now safe

`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:52` keeps
`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp/`. After the fix that form is served DIRECTLY over
https with no redirect, so the canonical URL is the safe one and stays consistent with the
`auth_resource_server_url` audience. Its test passes unchanged.

### NOT verified — read this before deploying

- **`nginx -t` was never run.** There is no nginx binary on this host and I did not install one.
  The config is verified **structurally only** (regex/brace parsing). Syntax validation is the
  operator's step at deploy time.
- **The live edge is unchanged.** Nothing was applied to the box; the 307 still reproduces in
  production right now. The LIVE VALIDATION acceptance criterion is deliberately unticked and
  requires an operator to deploy and evidence the actual response headers here.
- **Nothing was pushed.** The branch is local, 1 ahead / 2 behind `origin/main`.

### Residual risk

- Parity gap on `/review/`, `/opcert/` and Gerrit — **filed** as a61d-adf9-3725-4847
  (enchanting-phantastic-weevil), linked `discovered_from`.
- Root cause B's forward-looking trap (future code building URLs from the request rather than
  config) — **fixed in scope** by `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`, which is why B was fixed rather than
  only the edge.
- Process note: I used `git stash` in this worktree for the pre-fix/post-fix comparison. The
  stash stack is repo-global and other sessions had entries on it. Mine was popped and dropped
  and theirs were verified untouched, but `git diff > patch` + `git checkout --` would have been
  the correct tool and is what I used for the held-out oracle.

comments.body:
Operator-authorised production deploy of the nginx half of this fix — DONE and verified live (2026-08-27 ~22:05 UTC).

## The substitution mechanism (the thing the previous attempt could not find)

There is NO render script and NO automation. `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` is rendered by a
MANUAL OPERATOR STEP, and the recipe is documented in the template's own header (lines 4-12):

    export REVIEW_BOT_PORT
    envsubst '${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}' < infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template > /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf
    nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx

Exactly ONE variable is templated: `${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}`. The single-quoted envsubst argument is
load-bearing — it keeps nginx's own `$host` / `$remote_addr` / `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`
untouched. Copying the template verbatim is what produced the previous `unknown "review_bot_port"
variable` failure.

Value: `REVIEW_BOT_PORT=8000`, single-sourced at `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:225`
(`echo "REVIEW_BOT_PORT=8000"`) and by the compose default `${REVIEW_BOT_PORT:-8000}`
(`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:236`).

PROVEN, not guessed — on the box, rendering the CHECKED-OUT (pre-fix) template with
`REVIEW_BOT_PORT=8000` produced a file byte-identical to the live `/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf`:

    diff /tmp/render_test.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf  ->  IDENTICAL

Why nothing automates it: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` deliberately never re-renders
`conf.d/rebar.conf`. It only materialises the two GLOB-included files —
`/etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` (the blue-green upstream flip seam) and
`/etc/nginx/opcert-guard*.conf` — and reloads nginx. So this manual install will NOT be reverted
by autodeploy, and equally will NOT be applied to a rebuilt box automatically.

## What was deployed

- Backup: `/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf.pre-79b2-fix.1787868326.bak` (sha256 verified equal to the
  pre-change live file: `baf0c908e45a...`).
- Rendered `e9cec6bad8d1`'s template with `REVIEW_BOT_PORT=8000` -> 231 lines.
- Pre-install sanity gate passed: >200 lines, contains `location = /mcp/`, contains
  `Strict-Transport-Security`, contains `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000/;`, no unsubstituted `${`.
- `nginx -t` exit code captured DIRECTLY (`nginx -t > out 2>&1; RC=$?`), not through a pipeline —
  the previous attempt's `if nginx -t | tail -2; then` guard could never fail because a pipeline
  reports `tail`'s status. RC=0, "syntax is ok / test is successful".
- `nginx -s reload` RC=0, nginx `active`.

Diff live->candidate was 86 lines and contained only this fix: the server-level HSTS `add_header`,
the two exact-match `location = /mcp/` and `location = /mcp` blocks proxying to
`http://rebar_mcp/mcp`, and the three `proxy_redirect http://... https://...` pairs.

## Live verification (from off-box)

BEFORE: `GET /mcp/` -> `HTTP/2 307`, `location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, no HSTS.

AFTER:
- `GET /mcp/`  -> 401, NO Location header at all, `strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`
- `POST /mcp/` -> 401, no Location, HSTS present (the real client verb; a 307 here is what would
  have replayed method+body+bearer over plaintext)
- `GET /mcp`   -> 401, unchanged, HSTS present
- `/review/health` -> 200 + HSTS (review-bot intact, port 8000 rendering correct)
- Gerrit `/` -> 200, `/login` -> 302 (intact)
- `/opcert/` -> 403 (fail-closed deny-all, intact)
- port 80 `/mcp/` -> 301 to https (intact)

The `www-authenticate` `resource_metadata` URL is https, as expected.

## Live now vs awaiting merge

LIVE NOW (manual install, this comment): part A (exact-match `/mcp/` + `/mcp` locations), part C
(server-level HSTS with `always`), and the `proxy_redirect` backstop.

STILL AWAITING CHANGE 2280 MERGE: part B, `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=*` on the mcp compose service.
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` IS in autodeploy's `MCP_PATHS`, so it deploys automatically on
merge via the blue-green path. The observed downgrade is gone without it, because nginx now maps
`/mcp/` onto the app's `/mcp` so Starlette is never asked to redirect; part B remains needed as the
forward-looking fix for absolute URLs the app builds from the request scheme.

Because the box's `/opt/rebar` checkout is at `d4a0a2a44` (pre-fix, 159-line template), the live
`rebar.conf` is now AHEAD of the box's checkout. When 2280 merges, autodeploy will fast-forward the
checkout but will still not re-render nginx — the live file already carries the fix, so they
converge. Anyone who re-renders from the template after the merge gets the same bytes.

## Deliberately not done

- Did not touch change 2280 or merge anything; the nginx install is out-of-band by design and the
  ticket's live-validation criterion is now evidenced.
- Did not use any force override.
- Pre-existing and NOT introduced here: `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` returns 404
  (it falls through to the Gerrit `location /`). The config has no such location before OR after
  this change — verified against the backup. Worth its own ticket; the MCP 401 advertises that URL.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The MCP client URL every doc and committed example specifies —
`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp/` (WITH trailing slash) — answers `307` with
`location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`: an HTTPS->HTTP downgrade, with no HSTS to
upgrade it back (the no-slash `/mcp` correctly 401s). A 307 preserves method and body,
and clients differ on whether they retain `Authorization` across a same-host scheme change, so
one that retains it puts its bearer PAT on the wire in plaintext — and the docs point AT the
affected form (`docs/mcp-client-setup.md:54`, `examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:18`).

## Confirmed root cause

Proven at runtime; evidence, the discriminating experiment and the attribution (caused_by
fd4a-4e91-f179-4932) are in the RCA comment. Three artifacts:

**A** `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:127` is a PREFIX `location /mcp` with a URI-preserving
`proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;`, so `/mcp/` reaches the app verbatim while it mounts at
`http_path = "/mcp"` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:524,618-627`); Starlette's `redirect_slashes`
emits the 307. `docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271` prescribes EXACT-MATCH locations here; the template
diverged.

**B** uvicorn is built at `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:311-317` with no `forwarded_allow_ips`, so
it defaults to `"127.0.0.1"` (`uvicorn/config.py:356-357`). The app runs in a container
(`docker-compose.yml:337`), so nginx arrives from the bridge gateway — untrusted — and
`X-Forwarded-Proto https` (`rebar.conf.template:132`) is dropped, making scheme-derived URLs
`http://`. Blast radius BOUNDED: RFC 9728 metadata comes from `auth_resource_server_url`
(`mcp_server.py:610`), served as `https`.

**C** The 443 server serves no `Strict-Transport-Security` header.

## Approach

1. **Serve `/mcp/` directly instead of redirecting.** Per `docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271`, add
   `location = /mcp/` and `location = /mcp`, both `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp/mcp;`, keeping
   the SSE settings. A URI on `proxy_pass` replaces the matched URI, so `/mcp/` arrives as
   `/mcp`, `redirect_slashes` never fires, and no Location is produced. The PREFIX stays for
   sub-paths.
2. **Make a plaintext Location structurally impossible.** Add `proxy_redirect http://$host/
   https://$host/;` plus the named-upstream form to the MCP locations. Scoped there, not
   server-level: `proxy_redirect` defaults to `default` (derived from each location's own
   `proxy_pass`), so a server-wide rule would replace it for `/review/` and `/opcert/` and risk
   their relative redirects.
3. **Fix the scheme derivation.** Set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: "*"` on the `mcp` compose service.
   In uvicorn 0.52.1 a programmatic `Config` reads it from the environment
   (`uvicorn/config.py:356-357`) and wires `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` (`:527`), so no code change
   is needed. `"*"` not a pinned address: the `mcp` service declares no `networks:` block, so
   the gateway address is implicit and can drift, and a stale pin would re-open the downgrade
   while local tests passed. Trust-all is bounded — the port is on host loopback with nginx the
   sole client, setting `X-Forwarded-Proto https` as a LITERAL.
4. **Carry that env onto the blue-green deploy path.** `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` starts the
   MCP container with a bare `docker run` (`mcp_run_new`), not compose, so a compose-only env
   var never reaches a deployed container, leaving the fix inert on the path MCP ships through.
   Add the matching `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'` flag, a literal — `--env-file` supplies only
   what `.env` holds, and this value is a compose literal, not a `${...}` lookup — mirroring how
   `mcp_run_new` already carries the region vars.
5. **Add HSTS.** `add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
   always;` on the 443 server. `always` is required so it is emitted on error responses — such
   as the 401 MCP returns unauthenticated.

NOT changed: `EXPECTED_URL` in `test_mcp_client_configs.py` or the documented URLs — after step
1 the trailing-slash form is served over https, so it stays canonical.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The edge routes `/mcp/` straight to the app's `/mcp`, so no Location header is produced
      for the documented URL. Verified by a structural parse of `rebar.conf.template` asserting
      an exact-match `location = /mcp/` whose `proxy_pass` carries the path `/mcp`.
- [x] An HSTS header with `max-age` >= 31536000 is served on the 443 server, marked `always` so
      it reaches the unauthenticated 401. Verified by a structural parse asserting
      `add_header Strict-Transport-Security "..." always;` there.
- [x] Each MCP location carries a `proxy_redirect` mapping an `http://` upstream Location to
      `https://`. Verified by a structural parse that fails if any lacks it.
- [x] With the committed `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` in force, a `/mcp/` request through the real
      `streamable_http_app()` yields a Location whose scheme is `https`. Verified by an
      in-process ASGI test through `ProxyHeadersMiddleware`, with an untrusted-peer negative
      control asserting `http`, plus a structural check that compose sets it to exactly `*`.
- [x] The blue-green deploy path passes that same env to the container it starts:
      `autodeploy.sh`'s `mcp_run_new` carries `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'`. Verified by reading
      that function in the committed script. The existing parity test
      (`test_autodeploy_mcp_run_new_passes_the_bedrock_region`) asserts only `_MCP_REGION_VARS`;
      extending it to this var has no test yet and is tracked as follow-up.
- [x] [non-codebase] LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE. `curl -D -
      https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp/` emits no `http://` Location and carries HSTS,
      OBSERVED against the deployed edge. Not determinable from source, so an OPERATOR must
      apply the config.
      provenance: environment=production nginx edge at rebar.solutions.navateam.com; principal=unauthenticated caller (no credential sent); privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — GET and POST of /mcp/ both returned HTTP/2 401 with NO Location header and strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, so the 307 downgrade is gone.

## Testing

RED-first; both tiers observed failing before any fix.

## Compat / rollback

Additive: two exact-match locations ahead of the retained prefix, two directives per MCP
location, one HSTS header, one compose env var and its `docker run` flag. `/mcp` still
returns 401; `/mcp/` stops redirecting and serves. No caller depends on the 307 — it is the
defect. Rollback reverts the five files.

## Portability

Committed config plus tests that parse committed text. No CI provider is involved: the
structural tests run under plain `pytest` and the behavioural test is in-process ASGI, with no
docker and no network. Applying the nginx change is an operator step, not a CI trigger.
